opportunity.title: FEMA's Deployment Management Solution (Sources Sought)
opportunity.description: FEMA is conducting market research for commercial off-the-shelf, configurable COTS, custom or hybrid solutions to replace the legacy Deployment Tracking System and improve incident workforce management: readiness, personnel availability, qualifications, certifications, training, deployment tracking, incident and event staffing, force packages, equipment assignment, reporting and analytics, secure cloud hosting, and interoperability with FEMA and DHS systems. Estimated value is $50 million to $100 million over five to ten years. Questions were due Oct 5, 2026.

profile._note: FICTIONAL SAMPLE COMPANY for scenario testing. Not a real firm. Past performance and staffing are invented; only the NAICS codes, set-aside definitions and every opportunity and award figure used against it are real public data.
profile.name: Magnolia Women's Analytics LLC (sample)
profile.pastPerformance: Women-owned, economically disadvantaged. One Marine Corps training-data contract (about $1.5M) and two civilian-agency analytics task orders under $800K.
profile.capacityNotes: Eleven staff. No facility clearance. Past performance is strongest in training and education data systems.
verification: NAICS codes confirmed against USAspending reference (api.usaspending.gov/api/v2/references/naics) on 2026-10-16.
Set-asides follow SBA definitions: SBA = small business, 8A = 8(a) Business Development, HUBZONE, WOSB/EDWOSB, SDVOSB.

checks.reason: Full and open competition; no set-aside required.
NAICS 541511 is in the company's codes.

rationale.point: The opportunity is a Sources Sought for market research on replacing FEMA's Deployment Tracking System, not a formal solicitation; responding could help shape requirements toward a scope that fits Magnolia's training-data analytics experience.

Historical DHS awards under NAICS 541511 show a median top award of $47.3M with only 153 of 1,187 awards having a small-business set-aside, indicating the eventual contract will likely be large and full-and-open — beyond Magnolia's 11-person capacity and $1.5M max past performance.

risks: Eventual solicitation may be unrestricted and too large for a small firm with no facility clearance.
Magnolia's past performance is in training/education data systems, not incident workforce management or deployment tracking.
No small-business or WOSB/EDWOSB set-aside is indicated for the follow-on contract.
nextSteps: Submit a capabilities response to the Sources Sought highlighting relevant analytics and training-data experience to influence acquisition strategy.
Monitor for the formal solicitation; only bid if a small-business or WOSB/EDWOSB set-aside is applied or if the scope is broken into smaller task orders.
Explore teaming with a larger prime that has deployment-management past performance.
